label: Presidential Approval Rating
deltaNote: Peaked at 85% Feb 2025; fell to 72% Mar 2026; 54% Mar 2026; 51% end-April; dipped below 50% for the first time in early July amid inflation/purchasing-power concerns; rebounded to 57% by Aug 6 as headline inflation fell to 3.12% (lowest since May 2020) and Sheinbaum sharpened criticism of ICE following the July 7 Houston killing of Lorenzo Salgado Araujo. Pollster divergence widened later in August: SRC's Aug measurement put her at 55.5% approval / 44.5% disapproval — her lowest of the year by that firm's methodology — while MetricsMx (Aug 26) showed 73.0% and CB GlobalData's international comparison (Aug) showed 66.5%, second-highest in Latin America.

label: Homicide Rate (per 100k)
source: SNSP / INEGI; García Harfuch security balance, H1 2026 report; Sheinbaum Second Government Report, September 1, 2026
contestNote: H1 2026 (Jan–Jun): 8,988 homicides nationally, daily avg 49.7 — down 30.1% vs. same period 2025. June alone averaged 45.4/day, the lowest June in 12 years and a 48% drop since Sept 2024. At her September 1 Second Government Report, Sheinbaum reiterated the 51% drop in the daily homicide average since the start of her term (also framed as ~44 fewer deaths/day) alongside a 32% drop in high-impact crimes, 63,000 people detained for crimes since Oct 2024, 207 priority-target arrests, 32,824 firearms and 519 tonnes of drugs seized, and 2,725 clandestine labs dismantled. 54% of homicides concentrated in 8 states led by Guanajuato, Baja California, and Chihuahua; homicides fell in 29 of 32 states (only Oaxaca, Colima, Tlaxcala rose). PAN and PRI disputed the overall security narrative at the Sept 1 report, citing continued disappearances and the Aug 30 Ojocaliente, Zacatecas car-bomb attack (17th explosive-device attack on security forces in the state in two years). Critics note: disappearances still rising; Sinaloa cartel conflict ongoing; independent analysts warn of potential reclassification effects.
delta: -51% in daily average homicides since Sept 2024 (~44 fewer deaths/day), per Sept 1 Second Government Report

label: GDP Growth (Q1 2026 / Q2 2026 / 2026 full-year forecast)
source: INEGI Q2 2026 preliminary (July 30) and as revised in Sheinbaum's Second Government Report (Sept 1); OECD Economic Outlook June 3, 2026; Citi Encuesta de Expectativas May 21, 2026
contestNote: Q1 2026: -0.8% QoQ, +0.2% annual (all sectors declined). Q2 2026 preliminary release (July 30) showed +2.1% YoY / +1.5% QoQ; Sheinbaum's September 1 Second Government Report cited a revised +1.9% YoY / +1.4% QoQ for the same quarter — still the strongest quarterly rebound since Q4 2020, boosted by World Cup-related consumer/tourism spending. PAN opposition countered at the Sept 1 report that Sheinbaum's administration is averaging 0.8% growth vs. AMLO's 1.1%. delta: -475bp from 11.25% peak; held unchanged at both the June 2026 and August 6, 2026 meetings (5-0 vote in August). Board reiterated it is assessing the impact of prior cuts amid inflation now inside the 2.0–4.0% target range; no further cuts signaled.

label: Peso / USD Exchange Rate
source: FX markets / Banco de México reference rate, August 31, 2026
delta: Trading ~17.00–17.02 MXN/USD at the Aug 31 open, edging back to the 17-peso line for the first time since mid-August (peso appreciated 0.18% intraday, 3 centavos firmer than the Aug 28 close) after two weeks holding below 17; still up roughly 5.9% year-to-date from the 2025 close of 18.008. Year-end consensus remains 19.30–20.50 (SHCP 19.70, Banorte 19.30, Banxico survey analysts 20.00–20.50, Citi 19.50–20.20). Banxico rate at 6.50% continues to support carry trade.

label: Federal Budget Deficit (2024)
delta: Record high; fell to 4.9% of GDP in 2025 (short of the original 3.9% target). Per SHCP's Pre-Criterios 2027 (due to Congress by Sept 8), the deficit — measured as Public Sector Financial Requirements — is projected at 4.1% of GDP for 2026 and 3.5% for 2027, as Sheinbaum pledged "gradual" fiscal consolidation without cutting investment, health, education or welfare spending in her Sept 3 mañanera.
